source_refs.note: Topic 20.4.2 (PDF 70); the book's examples are redrawn. The book says the test distinguishes benzene with primary, secondary and tertiary alkyl groups; primary and secondary groups both have benzylic H and both react, so the lesson states what the test can show.

blocks.text: Oxidation of an alkyl group attached directly to a benzene ring is side-chain oxidation. Alkylbenzenes are readily oxidised by alkaline KMnO4, acidified K2Cr2O7 or dilute HNO3. The alkyl group, whatever its length, is oxidised to a carboxylic acid group, and the benzene ring is left intact: C6H5CH3 + 3[O] -> C6H5COOH + H2O (toluene to benzoic acid, on heating).

blocks.alt: Toluene + 3[O], with Heat over the arrow, gives benzoic acid (the ring carrying COOH) + H2O.
blocks.caption: Side-chain oxidation of toluene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 70).

items: The reaction needs at least one benzylic hydrogen, an H on the carbon attached to the ring. Without one there is no reaction, so a tertiary alkyl group on the ring is not oxidised.

However long the alkyl chain, the product has a single carboxyl group in its place, e.g. C6H5CH2R gives benzoic acid, and tetralin (a benzene ring fused to a saturated ring) gives benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid.

blocks.alt: Three reactions with KMnO4 over and H+ under the arrow: a benzene ring carrying CH2-R gives the ring carrying C(=O)OH; tetralin, a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring, gives a benzene ring with two C(=O)OH groups on neighbouring carbons; a benzene ring carrying CR3 gives No Reaction.
blocks.caption: Side-chain oxidation with KMnO4 (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 70).

items: Alkanes and benzene are each very resistant to oxidation, but in an alkylbenzene the benzylic carbon becomes reactive and easily oxidised.

blocks.text: Oxidation by KMnO4 is used as a test: the purple colour of KMnO4 disappears when it is used up in oxidising an alkylbenzene that has a benzylic hydrogen. Benzene and tertiary alkylbenzenes leave the colour unchanged.
